note.note:
History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute severe left-sided headache that woke the patient from sleep this morning (~05:30); persistent since then.
- Onset/duration/progression: Began on awakening today (~05:30); present at time of consultation; started suddenly enough to awaken patient.
- Character/associated symptoms: Described as "really horrible" and headachy; mild photophobia (bright lights make eyes sore); transient dizziness on waking that has since subsided; no nausea/vomiting; no neck stiffness; no fever.
- Triggers/context: Several months of increased work-related stress and late nights; normally sleeps later (~07:00) but woke early; history of prior headaches (less severe, typically frontal/bilateral rather than unilateral).
- Response to treatment: Took paracetamol this morning with little benefit.
- Social: Lives with partner; non-smoker; runs ~3×/week; has a cat.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: Anxiety diagnosed ~2 years ago.
- Medications: Sertraline — dose/route/frequency not documented. Paracetamol taken this morning — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: None reported / "Not that I'm aware of."
- Past hospitalizations/surgeries: Not recorded.
- Family history: No family history of diagnosed migraine or major physical illnesses; mother has history of anxiety.

Physical Examination:
- Physical exam: No formal physical examination or vital signs recorded during this consultation (Not recorded).
- Reported/observed findings (patient report):
  - Left-sided severe headache, persistent since waking.
  - Mild photophobia (lights make eyes sore).
  - Transient dizziness on waking that improved.
  - No neck stiffness.
  - No fever.
  - No nausea or vomiting.
  - Headache initially uncomfortable when lying down but overall somewhat better when lying down.
- Relevant negatives: No reported focal neurological deficits, no collapse/syncope, no marked photophobia/phonophobia beyond mild eye soreness.

Impression:
- One-line clinical impression: Probable primary headache — tension-type headache most likely; migraine is a plausible alternative.
- DDx (consistent with transcript) — top plausible diagnoses:
  - Tension-type headache: Likely given chronic work-related stress, anxiety history, late nights; consistent with the clinician's assessment.
  - Migraine: Possible because of unilateral pain and mild photophobia and common triggers present (stress, sleep disturbance).
  - Headache related to sleep deprivation/dehydration: Plausible contributing factor given late nights and clinician advice.

Management Plan:
- Immediate/acute treatment advised:
  - Start ibuprofen for headache (dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript).
  - Continue paracetamol if desired (patient already took paracetamol this morning; dose not documented).
- Symptomatic/self-care advice:
  - Ensure 7–8 hours sleep per night.
  - Drink 1.5–2.0 L of fluids daily (excluding tea/coffee).
  - Consider taking time off work (suggestion: up to one week; self-certify) to reduce stress.
  - Consider accessing local counselling service (doctor will provide self-referral link).
- Safety-netting and escalation:
  - If symptoms worsen or new/worrying features develop (worse headache, sudden severe/worst-ever headache, neck stiffness, vomiting, focal neurological signs, collapse), contact services urgently / rebook earlier.
  - Doctor will include link to "danger signs" in the notes for patient review.
- Follow-up:
  - Planned follow-up in one week with same service/GP to reassess.
  - If no improvement at follow-up, consider blood tests or further investigations (e.g., imaging) as indicated.

Patient Summary:
- Patient woke at ~05:30 with a new, severe left-sided headache that has persisted despite paracetamol. Contributing factors likely include work-related stress, recent late nights, and possible sleep/dehydration effects. Plan is to start ibuprofen, optimize sleep and hydration, consider a short period off work, self-refer to counselling, and review in one week; escalate earlier if red flags develop.

Key Takeaways:
- Start ibuprofen for headache (dose not documented) and you may continue paracetamol if needed.
- Improve sleep (7–8 hours) and increase fluid intake (1.5–2 L/day) and consider short time off work to reduce stress.
- Seek urgent review if headache worsens, becomes sudden/"worst-ever", or if new neurological symptoms/fever/neck stiffness occur.

Next Steps:
- Patient to initiate ibuprofen and self-care measures today.
- Patient to self-refer to local counselling service (link to be provided in notes).
- Follow-up appointment arranged in ~1 week for reassessment.
- If no improvement at follow-up, clinician to consider blood tests and/or imaging.
- Patient to contact service sooner if symptoms worsen or red flags appear.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (BP, HR, temperature) — Not recorded.
  - Neurological and focused physical examination (including fundoscopy, cranial nerve/limb exam) — Not recorded.
  - Exact medication details: sertraline dose/route/frequency not documented; paracetamol dose not documented; ibuprofen dose/route/frequency recommended but not documented.
  - Alcohol/caffeine intake details not documented.
  - Past hospitalizations/surgeries not documented.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None noted — DDx is consistent with transcript reasoning.
- Transcript quality:
  - Good quality and audible; clinician and patient history clearly documented with minimal background noise.
